title: A round's window shows what the crew member is doing, readably formatted, and a dashboard shows every live round
public_title: Show crew rounds as a readable live view
acceptance: Why. When a worker or reviewer round runs, the captain can watch it in a terminal window (a Herdr tab, a cmux workspace or a tmux window) or with `bin/fm.sh follow <actor>`. Today both copy the round's raw log file, `run.log`, byte for byte with `tail -f` behaviour (`follow()` in `bin/fm-herdr.py`, about line 819). For a codex round that log is one JSON object per line, so a person sees long JSON records instead of the commands the model ran, the files it changed and what it said. For claude, cursor-agent and gemini rounds the log stays silent until the very end, apart from a heartbeat line, so a healthy round looks stuck. The captain asked for a view that shows what each crew member is doing right now, with readable formatting and highlighting.

How. The window keeps running the same command it runs today, `fm-herdr.py follow <attempt>` (built in `bin/fm-herdr.py` about line 1546), so no window, transport or host code changes. Only what `follow` prints changes. A new module, `bin/lib/fm_follow_view.py`, reads the same `run.log` and turns it into readable output. `fm-herdr.py` imports it lazily inside `follow`, and when the module is missing (some test fixtures copy only `fm-herdr.py`, for example `tests/lib/herdr.py` about line 826) it falls back to today's raw copy.

Read-only. The viewer runs outside the round's sandbox (the operating-system jail a round runs in) and only reads. It never creates or changes a file in the round's attempt directory, the actor directory, the worktree, `state/` or the code snapshot, and it writes no Python bytecode (`sys.dont_write_bytecode` is set before the import). Today's liveness check, `round_live` (about line 870), can create `execution.lock` through `execution_state`, so the viewer uses a new non-creating check that gives the same answer: it reads `runner.pid`, `execution.json` and the result and exit files, opens `execution.lock` read-only only if it already exists, and treats a missing lock as not held. Tests cover a missing lock file and a read-only attempt directory, and show that the attempt directory listing and modification times are unchanged after the viewer runs.

Header. The viewer starts with a header that names the actor, the task, the round number, the pull request, how long this attempt has run, and what the round is doing now (running a command, editing a file, writing a message, or waiting for the vendor). Sources, all local: actor, task, round and project from the actor's `identity.json` and the attempt's `invocation.json`; elapsed time from the modification time of this attempt's `invocation.json`, so a fallback attempt (a second vendor tried after the first was unavailable) counts from its own start. The pull request comes from the newest event in the event log that belongs to this task and this project and carries a `pr` field; an event with no `project` field counts as the default project's, the same rule the existing reader uses (`bin/fm-herdr.py` about line 395). The event log is the one beside the attempt's own record root (the attempt lives under `<root>/state/runs/<actor>/<attempt>`, so the log is `<root>/state/events.jsonl`), which also holds for `follow <attempt>` and for routed external records. With no such event the header says `no PR yet`. A missing value, for example in an attempt recorded before this change, is shown as `unknown`. On a terminal the header stays at the top and refreshes once a second; otherwise it is printed once at the start.

Commands. Each command the model runs is shown as one line, `$ <command>`, and when it finishes its exit code, green for 0 and red otherwise. Output is collapsed to its first N and last N lines with a line that says how many lines were hidden; output of 2N lines or fewer is shown whole. N is 5 by default. `FM_FOLLOW_LINES=<N>` sets both limits; N must be a whole number from 1 to 200, and any other value keeps 5 and prints one warning line.

File changes. When the model changes a file, the viewer shows that file's change against the round's last commit (`HEAD`), staged and unstaged together, as a unified diff (the `+`/`-` line format of `git diff`), with added lines green and removed lines red, labelled as the file's state now, because it may have changed again since the event. Tracked files use the `git diff` command in the next requirement. A new untracked file is shown with the same flags as `git diff --no-index -- /dev/null <path>`, so as all added lines. A deleted file is shown as all removed lines. Rename detection is turned off (`-c diff.renames=false`), so a rename shows as one deletion and one addition, each path labelled, whatever the repository configures. A binary file is one line saying it changed. A worktree or path that no longer exists, or a git error, is one line `diff unavailable: <reason>`.

No side effects from git, and built-in highlighting only. The viewer runs git as `git --no-optional-locks -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.pager=cat -c diff.renames=false -C <worktree> diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color HEAD -- <path>` (and the `--no-index` form for untracked files) with `GIT_PAGER=cat`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` and an empty `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL`, so a repository setting cannot start an external diff program, a text converter, a filesystem monitor, a pager or a network fetch, and no lock is taken. Besides git, the viewer runs only `ps`, read-only and exactly as today's liveness helpers do (`process_matches` and `group_live` in `bin/fm-herdr.py`, about lines 863 to 899 and 1894), to see whether the round's processes are alive; it runs nothing else. Syntax highlighting is its own, by file extension, for Python, shell, TypeScript and JavaScript, JSON and Markdown (keywords, strings, comments and numbers in distinct colours), and plain colouring for any other file. It does not call `delta`, `bat` or any other highlighter, so no outside program can write files or reach the network. Tests plant a hostile repository configuration (external diff, text converter, filesystem monitor and pager, each of which would create a marker file) and show that no marker appears. A test also records every program the viewer starts, through stub `git` and `ps` earlier on `PATH` that log their arguments and then run the real ones, plus stub `delta`, `bat`, `gh` and `curl` that create a marker file, and shows that only `git` and `ps` ran, with the arguments above.

Messages. Text the model writes to explain itself is wrapped to the terminal width and set apart from command output by its own colour and a leading marker. The sources are the same fields the final-answer reader already uses (`bin/fm-herdr.py` about lines 1795 and 1808): codex `agent_message` items' `text`, claude and cursor-agent `result`, and gemini `response`. The viewer only displays them; the authenticated final-answer extraction is unchanged.

Status lines. The viewer shows single marked lines for these records, and only these: from `run.log`, the round started, heartbeat, and finished with its exit code (`bin/fm-herdr.py` about lines 1838 to 1848) and the sandbox launcher's notices; from the event log (found as in the header requirement, read only), the events this actor emitted, such as brief coverage, ASK, commit pushed and pull request opened. No producer changes: `bin/fm-worker.sh` and `bin/fm-review.sh` keep writing what they write today. A window ends at its existing boundary, when the round's result is written (`bin/fm-herdr.py` about line 1591), which is before the worker publishes; so a window shows only events emitted up to its end, and publication events after that are intentionally absent from it. `bin/fm.sh follow <actor>` started on a round that has already finished prints the whole log, then every event of that actor recorded so far, then exits. A test shows a post-completion `commit_pushed` event absent from the window's output and present in a later manual follow.

Vendor buffering. The viewer tracks vendor silence: how long it has watched the log without a new line that is not a heartbeat. Log lines carry no timestamps, so silence before the viewer attached cannot be known; it starts at zero when the viewer attaches and the value is shown as `unknown` until the viewer has watched for `FM_FOLLOW_QUIET` seconds (default 30). When the round is alive and observed silence passes that value, the viewer shows `waiting for <vendor>: it sends its output when it finishes (<observed time>)`, so a quiet round does not look stuck. This does not depend on the heartbeat interval (`FM_HEARTBEAT_SECS`, which can be 0 to turn heartbeats off). It is the normal state for claude, cursor-agent and gemini rounds, whose adapters ask for one final JSON result. Tests attach late to a running fixture round, once with heartbeats continuing and once with heartbeats off, and check the `unknown` start and the switch to the waiting line.

Log formats. The viewer understands every adapter's log, with recorded `run.log` samples as fixtures: codex JSON events (`thread.started`, `turn.started`, `turn.completed`, and `item.started` / `item.completed` for `command_execution`, `file_change`, `agent_message` and `web_search`, shown as one line `search: <query>`); the single final JSON object of claude and cursor-agent (`result`) and gemini (`response`); the mock adapter's text; and plain text lines from firstmate and the sandbox launcher. A line it cannot parse is printed as plain text. A partial last line is held until its newline arrives or the round ends, then printed once, never twice. None of this changes an adapter's output flags.

Plain output and sanitizing. Colour and screen control are used only when standard output is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is not set. Otherwise the viewer prints the same content as plain text, and every log-derived string has escape sequences and other control characters except newline and tab removed, in both coloured and plain output. Status lines keep their original words, so checks such as `started on T-035` and `finished exit=0` (`tests/herdr/windows.py` about line 540) still pass. The one exception is the heartbeat: on a terminal it updates one line in place; in plain output it is printed at most once every 60 seconds.
Raw mode. `bin/fm.sh follow <actor> --raw`, `fm-herdr.py follow <attempt> --raw` and `FM_FOLLOW_RAW=1` keep today's byte-for-byte copy of the log, with no sanitizing, for debugging the viewer itself.

Dashboard. `bin/fm.sh follow --all` (with the existing `--project` and `--repo` options) shows one line per live round of the selected project, found through the same routed record root that `fm.sh follow <actor>` uses today. For each actor it takes the latest attempt. It shows actor, task, elapsed time, current activity, log age (time since `run.log` last changed) and vendor silence (as defined above). On a terminal it refreshes every 2 seconds until Ctrl-C, and marks a round as possibly stuck once its observed vendor silence exceeds `FM_FOLLOW_STUCK` seconds (default 300), whatever the heartbeats do. When the output is not a terminal it prints one snapshot and exits 0; a snapshot cannot observe silence, so it shows vendor silence as `unknown` and marks no round as stuck. A round counts as live by the read-only liveness check above; an attempt with no `runner.pid` is shown as `starting` within the follower start grace and left out after it; finished attempts are left out. With no live round it prints `no live rounds`.

Ending. The single-round viewer ends exactly when today's follower ends: a `result.json` or `runner.exit` file appears, or nothing of the round is left running, including a killed runner whose adapter group survives (`tests/herdr/handoff.py` about line 37), and after the start grace `FM_FOLLOW_GRACE` (default 120 seconds) when no round ever started. Closing its window stops nothing.

Language. The terminal viewer is command-line output like the rest of `bin/`, so its labels are English only and not in the i18n dictionaries (§9 covers the board and cards). The §11 text states this boundary, and a test checks that every label comes from the viewer's fixed English table.

Privacy. For an external project (`FM_EXTERNAL=1`, records routed to the project's private storage) the viewer shows only what that round's `run.log`, events and worktree already hold on the captain's machine. It writes nothing, sends nothing over the network, and adds nothing to events, wakes, pull requests or the board. A test with routed external storage checks that no file under the private storage, the worktree or the cache changes, and that stub `gh`, `curl` and git network transports are never called.

Tests, new behaviour. A new suite, `tests/follow-view.test.sh` with its helper `tests/lib/follow_view.py`, drives the viewer only through the existing command-line entry points (`bin/fm.sh follow` and `bin/fm-herdr.py follow <attempt>`), which exist on the current base, never by importing the new module. Each formatting assertion is named and fails on the current base because base prints raw JSON or rejects the new option, which is a behavioural failure, not a setup error. Named assertions include: the `$ <command>` line; the exit code marker; collapsed output with the hidden-line count; one diff each for a staged change, an unstaged change, a new untracked file, a deleted file, a rename shown as deletion plus addition with both paths (also with `diff.renames=true` configured in the repository), a binary file and an unavailable path; the message marker; the buffering line; the PR in the header with same task IDs in two projects, a legacy event without `project`, and a routed external attempt; the dashboard line; and `--raw` and `--all` being accepted.

Tests, terminal behaviour. The suite runs the viewer in a pseudo-terminal (Python `pty`) to check the refreshing header, the in-place heartbeat line, wrapping at a set width, re-wrapping after a window resize signal, coloured versus `NO_COLOR` output, and that Ctrl-C ends the dashboard cleanly. It also covers `FM_FOLLOW_LINES` limits and invalid values, `FM_FOLLOW_QUIET` and `FM_FOLLOW_STUCK`, built-in highlighting for each supported file type and plain colouring for an unknown type, the hostile git configuration, legacy attempts with missing metadata, the read-only checks, every ending case above, and the external privacy case.

Tests, regressions. Behaviour the base already has is labelled regression, not new: the byte-for-byte raw copy, tolerance of unparseable lines, the ending rules, and the existing window and follower checks. These existing suites must pass unchanged and are not edited: `tests/herdr/windows.py`, `tests/cmux-window.test.sh`, `tests/herdr/handoff.py` (direct follower call about line 42), `tests/session.test.sh` (heartbeat producer about line 1021) with `tests/lib/session_heartbeat_fixture.py`, and the host and log fixtures in `tests/lib/herdr.py` (about lines 528 and 569).

Rollout. No record, pin, event, schema or stored-format change. Which view a follower shows depends on the code it runs, not on when it starts: a follower launched from code that contains this change shows the formatted view; a follower launched from an older frozen code snapshot, including a later fallback attempt of a task that started before the merge (it keeps that task's frozen `FM_CODE_ROOT`, `bin/fm-herdr.py` about lines 1511 to 1546), shows raw output as before. Old attempts that lack `identity.json` or some fields are shown with `unknown` values. Tests run one follower from a copy of the base code and one from current code on the same fixture attempt, show raw versus formatted output, and show records and pins unchanged.

Documentation. `design/design.md` §11, in the subsection 'Owners and wakes (T-151)' where it says the window runs `fm-herdr.py follow <attempt>` (about line 3736), describes the formatted view, raw mode, the dashboard, the read-only rule and the English-only boundary. `README.md` (about line 62) and `skills/firstmate/SKILL.md` (about line 203, where it says to watch a round with `bin/fm.sh follow <actor>`) mention `--all` and `--raw`. The `follow` help text in `bin/fm.sh` (about line 131) describes the new options.

Out of scope. No input box and no way to send text into a running round: that would break the sandbox and the authenticated final-answer rules. No change to how rounds start, run, stop or are sandboxed, to window creation, to adapters' output flags, or to `bin/fm-worker.sh` and `bin/fm-review.sh`.
